guarantees.claim: op_err is 1 when op_i is not equal to CIPH_FWD and not equal to CIPH_INV; otherwise 0.
cfg_valid is the logical AND of cfg_valid_i and the complement of op_err, so it is forced low whenever op_err is high.

assumptions.claim: op_i must be a deterministic logical value (0 or 1, no X) so that the equality checks produce a determinate result.
assumptions.risk: If op_i contains X, op_err becomes X, causing cfg_valid to be X, which may break assertions or downstream gating.

uncertain_points.claim: The comment states 'op_i is one-hot encoded' but the check only allows CIPH_FWD and CIPH_INV. If the ciph_op_e enum contains other legal values, they will be treated as errors, potentially blocking valid configuration.
uncertain_points.cond: op_i takes any value other than CIPH_FWD or CIPH_INV.
uncertain_points.risk: cfg_valid stays low even if cfg_valid_i is high, preventing assertion gating and possibly stalling configuration, which could be a functional bug if other op values are defined.
